We need to produce a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can have up to 9 capitalized words (all caps). Must wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. So output must start and end with a double quote character. Inside that, we have the resume text. Must ensure we don't accidentally include extra double quotes inside? Probably okay as long as the outermost are double quotes. We need to be careful not to include extra double quotes that could be interpreted as ending the string? The instruction: "Wrap the entire response with double quotation marks." So we should output a string that begins with " and ends with ". Inside we can have other quotes? Safer to avoid internal double quotes. Use single quotes if needed. Ensure capitalized words count <10. We'll use maybe 5 capitalized words: LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEM_SOLVING. Each capitalized word must be all caps. Underscore? Usually all caps letters only; underscores are not letters, but the word includes underscore, making it not pure letters? Might be considered not all caps because of underscore. Safer to use plain words without underscores: LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATAANALYSIS, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING. But those look odd. Better to use hyphen? Hyphen not letter. Could cause not all caps. Safer to use single words: LEADERSHIP, STRATEGY, ANALYTICS, COMMUNICATION, LEADERSHIP again? But we need distinct abilities maybe. Use: LEADERSHIP, STRATEGY, ANALYTICS, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING (still one word). Or we can use acronyms like SQL, HTML, etc. Those are all caps and count as words. Use maybe 6 capitalized words: SQL, HTML, CSS, JAVA, PYTHON, EXCEL. Those are all caps and count as words. That's 6 <10. Good.

Now produce resume with sections: Contact Info, Professional Summary, Skills (with capitalized words), Experience, Education, Certifications.

Make sure capitalized words appear less than 10 times total. We'll count each occurrence. We'll use each capitalized word maybe once. So total occurrences = number of capitalized words used. Use 6: SQL, HTML, CSS, JAVA, PYTHON, EXCEL. Ensure we don't accidentally repeat them. Use them in Skills section. Avoid using them elsewhere. Also avoid any other all caps words like "RESUME", "CURRICULUM", etc. Must avoid any other all caps words inadvertently. So be careful: headings like "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" are all caps, that would count. So we must not use all caps headings. Use normal case headings. So avoid any word that is all caps. Use title case or sentence case. Ensure we don't have any other all caps like "USA", "UK", "NA". Avoid those. Also avoid acronyms like "GPA". So we need to check.

Thus we will write resume with normal casing, except for the six skill words which are all caps. Ensure they appear exactly as those words, not as part of other words. Use them isolated.

Let's draft:

"Matthias Algiers
123 Example Street, Cityville, ST 12345
(555) 123-4567
matthias.algiers@email.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with over 5 years of experience in software development and data analysis. Proven ability to deliver high-quality solutions, collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, and drive projects to successful completion.

SKILLS
Programming Languages: JAVA, PYTHON
Web Technologies: HTML, CSS
Data Tools: SQL, EXCEL
Soft Skills: Leadership, Communication, Problem Solving

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Software Engineer, Tech Solutions Inc., Cityville, ST
June 2020 – Present
- Developed and maintained web applications using JAVA and PYTHON, improving system performance by 20%.
- Implemented responsive front-end interfaces with HTML and CSS, enhancing user engagement.
- Optimized database queries with SQL, reducing report generation time by 30%.
- Utilized EXCEL for data visualization and stakeholder reporting.
- Collaborated with agile teams to deliver projects on schedule and within budget.

Junior Developer, CodeCraft LLC., Cityville, ST
January 2018 – May 2020
- Assisted in building internal tools using JAVA and PYTHON.
- Created static web pages with HTML and CSS.
- Performed data extraction and transformation using SQL.
- Prepared monthly performance reports using EXCEL.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
State University, Cityville, ST
Graduated: May 2017

CERTIFICATIONS
Oracle Certified Associate, Java SE 8 Programmer
Microsoft Certified: Excel Associate
"

Now check for any all caps words besides the six. We have headings: "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" is all caps – that's a problem. Also "SKILLS", "PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE", "EDUCATION", "CERTIFICATIONS". Those are all caps and would increase count beyond limit. Must avoid any all caps headings. So we need to change headings to title case or sentence case, not all caps. Eg "Professional Summary", "Skills", "Professional Experience", "Education", "Certifications". Also ensure we don't accidentally have any other all caps like "USA", "ST" (state abbreviation) is two letters uppercase, that counts as all caps word. So we must avoid using state abbreviations like "ST". Use full state name or lowercase? Could use "State". But address line includes state abbreviation; we could write "State" spelled out. Or we could use lowercase "st"? But that looks odd. Better to write the state name fully, e.g., "New York". So avoid abbreviations.

Also phone number includes parentheses and digits, fine.

Email includes domain .com, not all caps.

Make sure not to accidentally have "SQL" inside other words like "SQL" is fine, it's our capitalized word. "HTML", "CSS", "JAVA", "PYTHON", "EXCEL". Those are our six.

Check for any other all caps: "Java" we wrote as "JAVA" only in skills. In experience we wrote "JAVA" and "PYTHON" etc. Must ensure we only use those six capitalized words exactly as they appear. In experience we wrote "JAVA" and "PYTHON". That's okay, they are part of the six. We used "JAVA" twice? Actually we used "JAVA" in skills and experience. That would increase count of occurrences. The constraint: "words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times." It refers to occurrences, not unique words. So total occurrences of any all caps word must be <10. We have six distinct words; if we repeat them, occurrences increase. We need total occurrences <10. We can afford some repeats but must stay under 10. Let's count.

We plan to use each maybe twice? Let's try to limit occurrences to maybe 6 total (one each). Use each only once in the resume. So we need to place each capitalized word only once. That means we cannot repeat them in multiple sections. We can place them all in the Skills section only, and not use them elsewhere. In experience, we must avoid using JAVA, PYTHON, etc. Instead we can describe using lowercase or other phrasing. Eg "developed applications using Java and Python" but that would have capitalized J and P? Actually "Java" and "Python" are capitalized first letter only, not all caps, so okay. However "Java" is not all caps because only first letter capital. "Python" same. So we can use those. Avoid "SQL" all caps; we can say "structured query language (SQL)"? That includes SQL all caps again. Better to avoid using the acronym; we can say "used structured query language for database queries". That avoids all caps. For Excel we can say "used spreadsheet software for data visualization". Avoid "EXCEL". For HTML and CSS we can say "used markup language and style sheets". Avoid all caps. So we will keep the six capitalized words only in the Skills section, each appearing once. Then total occurrences = 6 (<10). Good.

Now ensure we don't inadvertently have any other all caps words like "USA", "ST", "LLC", "Inc." etc. "LLC" is all caps; we must avoid. Use "Limited Liability Company" or just "Llc"? Better to avoid. "Inc." has capital I and period, but "Inc" is capitalized I followed by lowercase n c? Actually "Inc" is capital I then lowercase n c, not all caps. So "Inc." is okay because not all caps (I capital, n lower, c lower). "LLC" is all caps three letters, must avoid. So we need to rewrite company names without LLC all caps.
